introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) The resultant of the forces $(7\mathbf i-\mathbf j)$ N, $(x\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)$ N, $(-5\mathbf i+y\mathbf j)$ N and $(4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)$ N is $(10\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)$ N. Find the values of $x$ and $y$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The resultant is the vector sum of the forces:

$\mathbf i$-components: $7+x-5+4=10\Rightarrow x+6=10\Rightarrow x=4.$

$\mathbf j$-components: $-1+5+y+2=4\Rightarrow y+6=4\Rightarrow y=-2.$

Check: $(7\mathbf i-\mathbf j)+(4\mathbf i+5\mathbf j)+(-5\mathbf i-2\mathbf j)+(4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)=10\mathbf i+4\mathbf j$.

**$x=4$ and $y=-2$.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) A fifth force is introduced and the system of the four forces above (with resultant $(10\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)$ N) is now in equilibrium. Find the fifth force. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In equilibrium the total resultant is zero, so the fifth force $\mathbf F$ cancels the resultant of the other four:

$\mathbf F+(10\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)=\mathbf 0\Rightarrow\mathbf F=-10\mathbf i-4\mathbf j.$

**The fifth force is $(-10\mathbf i-4\mathbf j)$ N.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) Find the magnitude and direction of the fifth force, leaving your answer to one decimal place. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Magnitude: $|\mathbf F|=\sqrt{(-10)^2+(-4)^2}=\sqrt{116}=10.77\approx10.8$ N.

Direction: the force points in the third quadrant (both components negative). The acute angle with the negative $x$-axis is

$\alpha=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{10}\right)=21.8^\circ.$

**Magnitude $10.8$ N, directed $21.8^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis (opposite to the resultant), that is $201.8^\circ$ measured anticlockwise from the positive $x$-axis.**
themes: resultant of forces and equilibrium (additional maths)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii) A stone of mass 20 kg is thrown vertically upward to a height of 15 m. Find the work done against the weight of the stone. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The work done against the weight is the weight times the vertical distance risen:

$W=mgh=20\times10\times15=3000.$

**The work done against the weight of the stone is $3000$ J.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii) A car of mass 500 kg is travelling at a maximum speed of $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ on a rough hill inclined at $\sin\theta=\dfrac35$ to the horizontal. Given that the power exerted by the engine of the car is 36 kW, find the resistance to the motion. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances the forces opposing the motion. Take the car travelling **up** the hill.

Driving force: $P=Fv\Rightarrow F=\dfrac Pv=\dfrac{36\,000}{10}=3600$ N.

Component of the weight down the slope: $mg\sin\theta=500\times10\times\dfrac35=3000$ N.

Equation of motion along the slope (no acceleration):

$F-mg\sin\theta-R=0\Rightarrow R=3600-3000=600.$

**The resistance to the motion is $600$ N.**
themes: power and resistance of a vehicle
